items.title: Random fields, stationarity, covariance, and variograms
items.statement: Define a real random field on T subset R^d as a family of coordinate-measurable real random variables on one probability space, with joint measurability stated separately when needed for spatial integration. Define strict stationarity by shift-invariant finite-dimensional laws, wide stationarity by constant mean and covariance C(t-s), wide isotropy by covariance dependence only on ||t-s||, and order-two intrinsic stationarity by finite increment first and second moments depending only on displacement. Define gamma(h)=1/2 E[(X(s+h)-X(s))^2] for admissible s,h.

references.title: Evgeny Spodarev, Spatial Statistics: Lecture Notes (2024)
Evgeny Spodarev, Random Fields I: Lecture Notes (Draft, 2009)
Hermine Biermé, Introduction to random fields and scale invariance: Lecture I (2016)

items.title: Covariance kernels of square-integrable fields are positive semidefinite
items.statement: For any real random field whose coordinates are square-integrable, its covariance kernel K(s,t)=Cov(X(s),X(t)) is symmetric and positive semidefinite: every finite real quadratic form sum_{i,j} a_i a_j K(s_i,s_j) is nonnegative.

references.title: Evgeny Spodarev, Spatial Statistics: Lecture Notes (2024)
Hermine Biermé, Introduction to random fields and scale invariance: Lecture I (2016)

items.title: Gaussian field existence from a mean and a positive-semidefinite kernel
items.statement: Assume AC. For T⊆R^d with d≥1, mean function m:T->R, and symmetric positive-semidefinite kernel K:T×T->R, the Gaussian finite-dimensional laws N_|F|(m_F,K_F) are consistent and Kolmogorov extension gives a unique probability law on the cylinder sigma-algebra of R^T with those marginals. The coordinate field has mean m and covariance K; no path continuity, sample regularity, or joint measurability is asserted.

references.title: Evgeny Spodarev, Spatial Statistics: Lecture Notes (2024)
Evgeny Spodarev, Random Fields I: Lecture Notes (Draft, 2009)

items.title: Order-two intrinsic variograms are conditionally negative definite
items.statement: For an order-two intrinsically stationary real field on R^d, gamma(h)=1/2 E[(X(s+h)-X(s))^2] is independent of s. If the field is also wide stationary with covariance C(h), then gamma(h)=C(0)-C(h). For every finite set of sites s_i and real coefficients a_i with sum_i a_i=0, sum_{i,j} a_i a_j gamma(s_i-s_j)<=0. This CND conclusion is choice-free.

items.title: Bochner spectral measure of a continuous stationary field covariance
items.statement: Assume AC and DC. Let X be a real wide-stationary field indexed by R^d with continuous covariance C(h)=Cov(X(t),X(t+h)). On the usual locally compact Hausdorff additive group G=R^d, there is a unique finite positive Radon measure mu on the Pontryagin dual G-hat such that C(h)=integral_G-hat chi(h) mu(d chi) for all h; mu(G-hat)=C(0). This is a measure representation and makes no density assertion.

items.title: A failed stationary covariance and a valid quadratic variogram
items.statement: The function C(h)=1+h^2 is not a stationary covariance on R, while gamma(h)=h^2 is an order-two intrinsic variogram, witnessed by X(t)=tZ with a centered two-point random variable Z of second moment 2. The example also verifies the real zero-sum CND inequality for h^2 and shows the witness is not wide stationary.
